# BookJumpr

> BookJumpr (https://bookjumpr.com) maps the books mentioned inside other books: when a character reads one, quotes one, or name-drops one. 5,401 books, 7,802 mentions, most with the line where the mention happens. Last updated 2026-10-14.

Each book has a page at https://bookjumpr.com/<author-slug>/<title-slug> listing every book it mentions (with the line) and every book that mentions it; each author has a page at https://bookjumpr.com/<author-slug>.

## Key pages

- [Home](https://bookjumpr.com/): search any book and browse the network
- [The most-mentioned books](https://bookjumpr.com/stats): books ranked by how many other books mention them
- [About](https://bookjumpr.com/about): how mentions are collected and what counts as one
- [Network](https://bookjumpr.com/network): every book as one map of who mentions whom
- [Example book page: Norwegian Wood](https://bookjumpr.com/haruki-murakami/norwegian-wood): the books Murakami's novel mentions, with quotes

## Example connections

- [Norwegian Wood](https://bookjumpr.com/haruki-murakami/norwegian-wood) (Haruki Murakami) mentions [The Catcher in the Rye](https://bookjumpr.com/j-d-salinger/the-catcher-in-the-rye): "No War and Peace, no Kenzaburo Oe, no Catcher in the Rye."
- [Brave New World](https://bookjumpr.com/aldous-huxley/brave-new-world) (Aldous Huxley) mentions [Romeo and Juliet](https://bookjumpr.com/william-shakespeare/romeo-and-juliet): "Upstairs in his room the Savage was reading Romeo and Juliet."
- [Franny and Zooey](https://bookjumpr.com/j-d-salinger/franny-and-zooey) (J. D. Salinger) mentions [Peter Pan](https://bookjumpr.com/j-m-barrie/peter-pan): "Even before the curtain goes up at 'Peter Pan,' I'm a goddam puddle of tears."
- [The Catcher in the Rye](https://bookjumpr.com/j-d-salinger/the-catcher-in-the-rye) (J. D. Salinger) mentions [Oliver Twist](https://bookjumpr.com/charles-dickens/oliver-twist): "He's carrying this copy of Oliver Twist and so's she."
- [The Marriage Plot](https://bookjumpr.com/jeffrey-eugenides/the-marriage-plot) (Jeffrey Eugenides) mentions [Invisible Cities](https://bookjumpr.com/italo-calvino/invisible-cities): "a girl ... was smoking a clove cigarette and reading Invisible Cities"

## Questions BookJumpr answers

Q: What is BookJumpr?
A: BookJumpr (https://bookjumpr.com) is a free website that maps the books mentioned inside other books: when a character reads one, quotes one, or name-drops one. It covers 5,401 books and 7,802 mentions, most with the line where the mention happens.

Q: What is the most mentioned book in other books?
A: In BookJumpr's data, Don Quixote by Miguel de Cervantes is the book most often named inside other books (75 books), followed by Hamlet by William Shakespeare (71) and Robinson Crusoe by Daniel Defoe (63).

Q: Which books mention Don Quixote?
A: 75 books in BookJumpr mention Don Quixote by Miguel de Cervantes, including Adventures of Huckleberry Finn by Mark Twain; David Copperfield by Charles Dickens; The Count of Monte Cristo by Alexandre Dumas; The Three Musketeers by Alexandre Dumas; North and South by Elizabeth Gaskell; Tristram Shandy by Laurence Sterne; Main Street by Sinclair Lewis; The Idiot by Fyodor Dostoevsky; and 67 more. Full list: https://bookjumpr.com/miguel-de-cervantes/don-quixote

Q: Which books mention Hamlet?
A: 71 books in BookJumpr mention Hamlet by William Shakespeare, including Zero to One by Peter Thiel; The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy by Douglas Adams; The Art of Public Speaking by Dale Carnegie & J. Berg Esenwein; Night and Day by Virginia Woolf; On Heroes, Hero-Worship, and The Heroic in History by Thomas Carlyle; The Catcher in the Rye by J. D. Salinger; Adventures of Huckleberry Finn by Mark Twain; Kafka on the Shore by Haruki Murakami; and 63 more. Full list: https://bookjumpr.com/william-shakespeare/hamlet

Q: Which books mention Robinson Crusoe?
A: 63 books in BookJumpr mention Robinson Crusoe by Daniel Defoe, including The Autobiography of Benjamin Franklin by Benjamin Franklin; David Copperfield by Charles Dickens; The Moonstone by Wilkie Collins; North and South by Elizabeth Gaskell; Far from the Madding Crowd by Thomas Hardy; My Ántonia by Willa Cather; Bleak House by Charles Dickens; The Way We Live Now by Anthony Trollope; and 55 more. Full list: https://bookjumpr.com/daniel-defoe/robinson-crusoe

Q: What books are mentioned in Kafka on the Shore?
A: Kafka on the Shore by Haruki Murakami mentions 17 books: The Trial by Franz Kafka; The Metamorphosis by Franz Kafka; A Thousand and One Nights by Anonymous; The Miner by Natsume Sōseki; The Tale of Genji by Murasaki Shikibu; The Castle by Franz Kafka; In the Penal Colony by Franz Kafka; Poppies by Natsume Soseki; Kokoro by Natsume Sōseki; Sanshiro by Natsume Sōseki; Tales of Moonlight and Rain by Ueda Akinari; The Chrysanthemum Pledge by Ueda Akinari; and 5 more. With quotes: https://bookjumpr.com/haruki-murakami/kafka-on-the-shore

Q: What books are mentioned in Norwegian Wood?
A: Norwegian Wood by Haruki Murakami mentions 9 books: The Magic Mountain by Thomas Mann; Light in August by William Faulkner; The Centaur by John Updike; The Great Gatsby by F. Scott Fitzgerald; Lord Jim by Joseph Conrad; Beneath the Wheel by Hermann Hesse; Das Kapital by Karl Marx; War and Peace by Leo Tolstoy; The Catcher in the Rye by J. D. Salinger. With quotes: https://bookjumpr.com/haruki-murakami/norwegian-wood

Q: What books are mentioned in The Catcher in the Rye?
A: The Catcher in the Rye by J. D. Salinger mentions 13 books: David Copperfield by Charles Dickens; Out of Africa by Isak Dinesen; The Return of the Native by Thomas Hardy; Of Human Bondage by Somerset Maugham; Beowulf by Anonymous; Romeo and Juliet by William Shakespeare; Julius Caesar by William Shakespeare; A Farewell to Arms by Ernest Hemingway; The Great Gatsby by F. Scott Fitzgerald; Hamlet by William Shakespeare; Oliver Twist by Charles Dickens; Lord Randal, My Son by Traditional; and 1 more. With quotes: https://bookjumpr.com/j-d-salinger/the-catcher-in-the-rye

Q: What books are mentioned in Ulysses?
A: Ulysses by James Joyce mentions 30 books: The Tempest by William Shakespeare; Measure for Measure by William Shakespeare; The Maid's Tragedy by Francis Beaumont and John Fletcher; Hamlet by William Shakespeare; King Lear by William Shakespeare; Robinson Crusoe by Daniel Defoe; Romeo and Juliet by William Shakespeare; Antony and Cleopatra by William Shakespeare; Paradise Lost by John Milton; The Descent of Man by Charles Darwin; The Taming of the Shrew by William Shakespeare; The Woman in White by Wilkie Collins; and 18 more. With quotes: https://bookjumpr.com/james-joyce/ulysses
